account: A JBJS Case Connector report published 15 December 2021 (Jaime, Reif, Kafedzic, Garrison, Dhawan and Rozbruch) describes two people with traumatic transulnar amputations. Both underwent osseointegration implantation. After surgery a myoelectric prosthesis fitted with Coapt pattern-recognition software was attached directly to the implant. The software classifies electromyographic (EMG) signal patterns to drive a multiarticulating hand and wrist. Both trained with the software. At the most recent follow-ups of 18 months and 2 years the implants showed no loosening. The authors state that prosthetic control gradually improved to allow activities of daily living. Surgery dates are not given in the abstract.

ai_role.statement: The Coapt software is a machine-learning pattern-recognition controller that maps electromyographic patterns to hand and wrist motions. The report attributes improved control to training with this software on an osseointegrated attachment. So the AI contribution is entangled with the surgical attachment and cannot be isolated.

fields.account: A JBJS Case Connector report published 15 December 2021 (Jaime, Reif, Kafedzic, Garrison, Dhawan and Rozbruch) describes two people with traumatic transulnar amputations. Both underwent osseointegration implantation. After surgery a myoelectric prosthesis fitted with Coapt pattern-recognition software was attached directly to the implant. The software classifies electromyographic (EMG) signal patterns to drive a multiarticulating hand and wrist. Both trained with the software. At the most recent follow-ups of 18 months and 2 years the implants showed no loosening. The authors state that prosthetic control gradually improved to allow activities of daily living. Surgery dates are not given in the abstract.
